conventions.convention: Eigenvalues are ordered nonincreasingly with multiplicity; PCA component subspaces are full eigenspaces ordered by distinct eigenvalues. A tied leading eigenvalue defines the entire leading eigenspace.
Both PCA conventions center first. Correlation-PCA additionally divides by positive coordinate standard deviations; sample covariance uses divisor n rather than n−1.
The sine-angle is sqrt(1−(vᵀw)²), so eigenvector signs do not matter. The perturbation theorem assumes p≥2, a simple leading eigenvalue, gap g>0, symmetric perturbation, and operator norm ε<g/2.

Dimension and population law are fixed; the fourth moment is finite. Each sample is mutually iid, but probability spaces may differ with n. The root-n assertion means boundedness in probability after multiplication by sqrt(n).
The sample line angle is defined on G_n={ε_n<g/2} and extended by zero off G_n; uniqueness of the sample leading line is asserted with probability tending to one.
Calling sample covariance an estimator asserts measurability and matching target space, without asserting unbiasedness or consistency.

load_bearing.statement: Covariance-PCA is the ordered eigenspace decomposition of the centered covariance matrix. Correlation-PCA is the corresponding decomposition after standardization by positive coordinate standard deviations. Sample covariance-PCA uses sample-centered covariance with divisor n.

For symmetric A∈R^{p×p}, p≥2, with simple leading eigenvalue and gap g>0, a symmetric perturbation E with ε=||E||op<g/2 leaves the leading eigenvalue simple, changes it by at most ε, and gives sin angle(v,ṽ)≤ε/(g−ε) for any unit leading eigenvectors.

For fixed p≥1 and a fixed Borel law P on R^p with E_P||X||₂⁴<∞, an iid sample of size n has divisor-n sample-centered covariance satisfying ||Σ̂_n*−Σ||F=O_P(n^{-1/2}); the probability space may depend on n.

For a finite-second-moment vector in the PCA model and every unit a, Varθ(aᵀX)=aᵀΣθa. The maximum is λ₁(Σθ), attained exactly by unit vectors in the leading eigenspace. The same assertion holds for population-standardized coordinates when all coordinate variances are positive.

For the finite-second-moment iid Borel sample experiment, the divisor-n sample-centered covariance map T_n is a measurable statistic into the Borel space of symmetric matrices and hence an estimator of ψ(θ)=Σθ.

If a covariance matrix has λ₁=λ₂, its leading eigenspace ker(Σ−λ₁I) is uniquely specified and has dimension at least two; all its unit vectors are leading principal directions, without a distinguished unit vector.
